decisions.reason: Grounds attribution in contrast-probe.txt: file-trace's own RPC reads the same file, the documentpreview tab via the api-workspace-files Remote fails with meta.status stuck at 'none', so the read stalls in the metadata stage of the workspace-files resource-provider/RPC chain; it rules out disk existence, permissions and renderer, and notes the host row is declared but that declared/served does not prove the runtime chain took over.

Marks the per-module 62/62 HTTP 200 sweep and single-module probe as the valid measurement and the manually joined ~4 KB URL's 404 as a rejection of that URL form, not evidence of missing modules; explains the real loader fetches each manifest entry's own rev-tagged url instead of one all-in join. It treats the join as out-of-form/oversized (bounded partitioning) without inventing constants, and never invents a 60-vs-62 reconciliation.

Separates the paste-input fold warnings as an independent bug family unrelated to the resource read, and uses the boot manifest to explain the textpreview→documentpreview replacement whose canOpen now accepts session scope only — correctly attributing the absolute-address claim failure to that scope change and explicitly noting it cannot explain the session tab's stalled metadata.

Gives restart first, then rollback to the verified published 0.1.3-alpha.2 escape hatch from discussion #5999, then upstream follow-up in #5999 round 2; explicitly rejects plugin-side rewrite/retry/fallback as masking the host failure, and cites the alpha.1 #5999 round as prior art whose restart healed a roster/combo mismatch, without claiming alpha.2 still has missing bytes.

Packages versions/upgrade history, manifest, both probe outcomes with the invalid-join caveat, the same-file contrast with meta.status, console excerpt and #5999 round-2 reference for upstream; proposes concrete host diagnostics — a real boot-time meta round-trip probe per resource service and a resource-provider/Remote resolve check with workspaceRoot fallback verification — which is a specific failing-chain diagnostic rather than demanding an unseen health-check API.

caps.reason: The report explicitly rejects citing the oversized joined-URL 404 as proof of missing modules, calling that conclusion wrong against the 62/62 sweep; the bad interpretation appears only as a rejected example.
The report affirmatively rejects plugin-side rewrite/retry/fallback as a cure and proposes restart/rollback/upstream instead; no workaround or duplicate insertion is recommended.
